title.content: met with sarah and priya this morning about the Q3 onboarding revamp. current flow loses ~40% of signups before the first project gets created. decided: cut the legacy email drip entirely, replace the 6-step wizard with a single smart default workspace, and add an interactive checklist in the sidebar. sarah owns the checklist designs, priya is scoping the workspace templates. revisit metrics two weeks after launch. open question: do we grandfather existing trial users into the new flow or not?

overnight sourdough focaccia — 500g bread flour, 100g active starter, 400g water (80% hydration), 12g salt, big glug of olive oil. mix at 6pm, four sets of stretch and folds 30 min apart, then into the fridge overnight. morning: oil a 9x13 pan, dimple with wet fingers, top with rosemary and flaky salt, bake at 425F for 25-28 min until deep golden. notes from last attempt: bottom was pale — preheat a baking steel next time, and cut the salt to 10g, the olives already bring plenty.

spent the evening chasing the memory leak in the websocket relay. RSS climbs ~30MB/hour under steady load. heaptrack points at the per-connection broadcast buffers — we clone the payload bytes for every subscriber instead of sharing one allocation. tried switching to a shared Arc buffer and the growth flattened. still need to confirm the tokio task count isn't also creeping; tokio-console shows 4 orphaned tasks after reconnect storms. plan: land the Arc change, add a connection-close drop guard, rerun the 12h soak test.

actions.title: How HTTP caching works
actions.content: cache-control beats expires when both are present. max-age is relative to the response time; s-maxage only applies to shared caches. etag revalidation: the client sends if-none-match, the server replies 304 with no body when it matches. stale-while-revalidate serves the stale copy while refetching in the background. immutable tells the browser to skip revalidation entirely for the asset's lifetime.
